name: rails-default
description: Fallback rules for a Rails app with an RSpec suite and a Vite frontend. Array order decides which rule matches (first wins, so specific before general); `rank` decides reading order inside a weight.

rules.label: Migrations
rules.why: Runs once against production data and is awkward to undo.

rules.label: Authorization
rules.why: Decides who can do what. A mistake here is a security bug, not a bug report.

rules.label: Secret handling
rules.why: Controls what leaks into logs and error reports.

rules.label: Production config
rules.why: Applies to every request the moment it deploys.

rules.label: Edge / CDN
rules.why: Ships outside the normal pipeline, so the usual safety nets do not catch it.

rules.label: Dependencies
rules.why: New code from someone else. One line is still a supply-chain change.

rules.label: Credential fixtures
rules.why: Test support that handles real credential shapes. Check nothing live landed here.

rules.label: Translations
rules.why: Copy. Wrong wording is cheap to fix and reading 40 of them teaches nothing.

rules.label: Lockfiles
rules.why: Resolver output. The manifest above is the decision.

rules.label: Schema dump
rules.why: Generated by the migrations. Read those instead.

rules.label: API snapshot
rules.why: Generated from the request specs.

rules.label: Brakeman ignores
rules.why: Removing an entry means a warning was fixed; only additions need an argument.

rules.label: Factories and support
rules.why: Scaffolding for the tests. The tests themselves carry the meaning.

rules.label: Benchmarks
rules.why: Measurement scripts; they do not ship.

rules.label: Views and components
rules.why: Markup. Look at the shape; the browser is a better reviewer than you are.

rules.label: Frontend entrypoints
rules.why: Mounting and bundling glue.

rules.label: End-to-end tests
rules.why: Verbose by nature. Check what they assert, not how.

rules.label: Models
rules.why: The data contract. Associations, validations and scopes reach the whole app, so even a one-line change here is read.

rules.label: Controllers
rules.why: Where a request becomes an action: params, authorization calls, what gets rendered.

rules.label: Plugins
rules.why: Opt-in behaviour per brand. Check the boundary and what happens when it is disabled.

rules.label: Services, organizers and interactors
rules.why: The business logic. An organizer is the sequence; an interactor is one step and its rollback.

rules.label: API contract
rules.why: What clients already depend on. Breaking it is not a deploy you can take back.

rules.label: Routes
rules.why: New surface area, and the fastest place to spot something exposed by accident.

rules.label: Shared frontend
rules.why: Imported across entrypoints, so a change here is not local.

rules.label: Rake tasks
rules.why: Run by hand against production, usually once, usually under time pressure.

rules.label: Jobs and mailers
rules.why: Runs detached from the request. Check retries and what happens on partial failure.

rules.label: Docs
rules.why: Useful orientation, but the code is the source of truth.

rules.label: Migration specs
rules.why: Often the only check that a data backfill is correct.

rules.label: Request specs
rules.why: The contract as exercised. Read after the code they cover, as confirmation.

rules.label: Other application code
rules.why: The rest of the change.

rules.label: Unit specs
rules.why: Mostly restate the code above. Check the cases chosen, not the assertions.
